business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Magazine Publishing and Sponsored Media Placements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended by Law 7/2021 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing), Articles 3-4 for UBO definition and beneficial ownership disclosure; Royal Decree 304/2014 establishing the UBO Register; Law 1/2018 on the Protection of Personal Data and guarantee of digital rights.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Existence and Good Standing
Articles of Association and Incorporation Documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and Spanish sanctions screening using automated tools compliant with Law 10/2010; full adverse media and reputational checks on UBOs and directors.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (e-Registro Mercantil portal and associated commercial registries)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory Spanish language and Latin alphabet; foreign names must be transliterated into Spanish where required by notarial or registry formalities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusing with existing registered companies
Generic terms implying public services or monopolies without authorization
Names containing acronyms or abbreviations unless compliant with commercial code rules
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the relevant Commercial Registry Court within one month of rejection notice; subsequent judicial review before the Audiencia Provincial if administrative appeal fails.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada entities, particularly for digital publishing and media businesses; registered address must be verifiable but physical presence not statutorily required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5-10%) for digital magazine publishing sector; inspections primarily administrative or triggered by tax/compliance audits rather than routine incorporation verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July 2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, LSC): Arts. 20-33 (incorporation and nullity), Art. 59 (minimum capital of EUR 3,000), Arts. 60-62 (subscription, payment, deposit bank certificate and notarial deed), Art. 113 (registered office), Arts. 209-218 (administration); supplemented by the Spanish Commercial Code and Royal Decree 745/2006 on the organization and functioning of the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (for the negative name certificate) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (for inscription of the incorporation deed), supervised by the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública and coordinated by the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Mercantiles y de Bienes Muebles de España.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) granted before a Spanish notary, preceded by a certificación negativa de denominación social (negative name certificate), and registered with the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum capital for an S.L. is EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,300) fully subscribed and paid in cash before execution of the deed; payment is proven by a bank certificate of deposit in the name of the company in formation (Art. 62 LSC); Spanish law does not require an escrow account for this deposit; capital may not be fixed below the legal floor at incorporation, although a post-registration capital reduction to EUR 1 becomes available after two years of continuous registration (Art. 5 LSC); non-cash contributions, if any, require an independent expert valuation report (Art. 67 LSC).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the members hereby ratify the subscription and full payment in cash of the company's share capital of EUR 3,000, represented by 3,000 participations, as stated in the public deed of incorporation. (2) that the registered office of the company is fixed at the address specified in the bylaws, Madrid, Spain, and the administrator is instructed to file it with the Mercantile Registry. (3) that Mr./Ms. ________ is appointed Sole Administrator (Administrador Único) with all statutory powers of representation, management, and disposition. (4) that the Sole Administrator is authorized to open bank accounts, apply for the definitive NIF, register with the Social Security, execute digital publishing and advertising contracts, and otherwise complete the incorporation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Procurement of the negative company name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Madrid — online portal: www.rmc.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official request for a negative name certificate through the RMC online portal or its ordinary mail service. Specify that the company form will be S.L. (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) and provide up to three proposed corporate names ranked in order of preference. The certificate confirms that no existing Spanish company or trademark conflicts with the chosen name and is valid for three non-extendable months. The notarial deed must be executed within this validity window.
required_dossiers: Official application form for negative certification
Copy of the passport or NIE of the requesting party (or of its legal representative with notarized power of attorney)
Proof of payment of the official fee
List of the three proposed corporate names in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The RMC has no appeal mechanism against individual name refusals; the standard cure is to re-submit a new application listing alternative denominations. If a name is refused, the paid official fee is not refundable, so pre-checking existing denominations through the RMC query service is recommended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public deed of incorporation and adoption of the bylaws (otorgamiento de la escritura pública de constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (Notaría) in the district of the registered office chosen by the founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear in person before the notary, holding a valid NIE or passport (or a certified power of attorney for absent co-founders). Deliver the negative name certificate within its three-month validity, the bank certificate of deposit of the EUR 3,000 minimum capital in the name of the company in formation, the draft bylaws (estatutos), and, if any in-kind contribution is made, the independent valuation report under Art. 67 LSC. The notary verifies legal capacity and the legality of the bylaws clauses, reads the deed to the founders, and issues the first certified copy (primera copia) to be sent to the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate in force
Bank certificate of deposit of share capital (certificado bancario de desembolso)
Draft bylaws (estatutos) approved by all founders
Valid NIE or passport of each founder, or granted power of attorney
Independent expert valuation report if non-cash contributions are present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses the deed or conditions it on changes, the founders amend the draft bylaws to satisfy LSC Arts. 20-27 and re-sign the deed. The bank certificate may be re-issued if incomplete; there is no governmental appeal against a notarial refusal — the matter is cured by redrafting and a new notarial appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the provisional NIF and commencement of tax activity filing (Modelo 036)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — corresponding provincial delegation of the registered office (e.g., AEAT Delegación de Madrid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the deed is granted and before registry inscription, file Modelo 036 (censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) electronically or in person at the AEAT office, presenting the notarial certification, to obtain the provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional) of the company in formation. Also declare the commencement of business activity (inicio de actividad) and select the relevant IAE epigraph for editorial publishing services corresponding to the digital magazine portal.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 fully completed (draft 036/037)
First certified copy or notarial attestation of the deed of incorporation
NIE of the legal representative who signs the application, with an electronic certificate or granted power
Negative name certificate reference and provisional address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT formally requires corrections (data mismatch, unaccredited representative), the form is re-filed electronically with the electronic certificate or in person with the original authorization; re-filing is curable within 10 working days after the AEAT notice without additional sanction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Settlement of the capital-formation stamp duty (ITP-AJD, Modelo 600) with the regional treasury
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo (Dirección General de Tributos) of the Autonomous Community of the registered office (e.g., Comunidad de Madrid), through its regional tax e-registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Self-assess and pay the proportional stamp duty on capital operations (ITP-AJD, operaciones societarias) within 30 working days from the date of the deed. File Modelo 600 through the regional tax platform attaching the deed data; the payment receipt (justificante de liquidación) is required for the Mercantile Registry inscription and the definitive NIF procedure. The taxable base is the nominal capital subscribed, i.e. EUR 3,000, at the applicable autonomous rate (approximately 1%).
required_dossiers: Modelo 600 declaration drafted (dates, tax base, proportional rate)
Electronic copy or scan of the public deed
Provisional NIF of the company in formation and NIF/NIE of the declarant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or defective filing is cured by supplementary Modelo 600 filing with the applicable late-payment surcharges and interest under the General Taxation Law (Arts. 27 and 28 LGT); the corrected receipt can then be validated with the Mercantile Registry in the same procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the company in the Mercantile Registry (inscripción registral de la sociedad)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid), operated by Registradores de la Propiedad, Mercantiles y de Bienes Muebles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the Registro Mercantil Provincial the first certified copy of the incorporation deed, the Modelo 600 payment receipt, and proof of the provisional NIF. The registrar performs the legal admissibility review (calificación registral). Once entered, the company acquires separate legal personality under Art. 20 LSC; the registry issues the registration certificate (certificación) and the company's registry number (hoja registral), and the definitive NIF process is triggered.
required_dossiers: First certified copy of the deed (primera copia)
ITP-AJD (Modelo 600) liquidated receipt
Provisional NIF documentation
Negative name certificate if not already attached to the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar draws up a defect note (nota de calificación) withholding or suspending inscription, the founders can correct the defects and re-submit, or file an appeal against the calificación within the statutory deadline to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (gubernativo appeal). In practice, most initial defect notes are cured with a single corrective deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalization of incorporation: definitive NIF emission, employer registration with Social Security, and legalization of corporate books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (definitive NIF); Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS, employer code); Registro Mercantil Provincial (book legalization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once registry inscription is certified, submit the registration certificate to AEAT so the provisional NIF is converted into the definitive NIF; open a payroll and employer account (código de cuenta de cotización) with TGSS if the company intends to hire staff; and present the corporate books (shareholders registry and minutes book) to the Mercantile Registry for legalization, currently carried out digitally under the electronic book system. Also activate the company's electronic domicile (dirección electrónica habilitada) for official notifications.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registry inscription (certificación) or updated registry note
Provisional NIF number of the company
Modelo TA.6 / F.63 employer registration application with TGSS
Corporate books to be legalized (share register and minutes book) or digital legalization request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failures at this stage are cured by re-filing in the corresponding window: for the NIF conversion, update the AEAT register with the definitive registry certificate; for the TGSS, correct the applicant or financial data and re-tender the employer registration filing; for book legalization, repeat the request after meeting the format requirements of the electronic book regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal council of the registered office (Ayuntamiento) — area of urbanism and licensed activities; state or autonomous industrial licensing is NOT applicable to CNAE 5813 (digital magazine publishing) as it is a non-industrial tertiary activity with no manufacturing facilities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad (or municipal Licencia de Apertura where required by local ordinance) for administrative office premises only; no sector-specific media or broadcasting license is required for a digital magazine portal, and no physical production permit exists for this activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable — environmental competence rests with the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) and the regional environmental department of the Autonomous Community, but the activity falls outside the annexes of Ley 21/2013 on environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA report and no environmental registration required; the digital editorial activity emits no process pollutants and triggers no Annex I or Annex II category under Ley 21/2013.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable — no wastewater process discharge, no VOC or combustion emissions, and no hazardous waste generation; only general municipal solid-waste collection and WEEE obligations for office IT equipment apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance with Spanish fire safety regulations (RSCIEI and CTE-DBSI) and applicable municipal fire inspections for office premises; occupational health and safety under Ley 31/1995 (LPRL) requires a workplace risk assessment, employee safety measures, and, upon hiring initial workers, submission of the Comunicación de Apertura del Centro de Trabajo to the labor administration; no public-occupancy license is required for a closed digital office environment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal: https://www.agenciatributaria.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) obtains its definitive Corporate Tax Identification Number (NIF) through the formation process before the Commercial Registry and the AEAT. Foreign entities without a permanent establishment in Spain must appoint a fiscal representative and file the Spanish census registration Form 036/037 with the AEAT to obtain an NIF for non-resident entities. Entities with a permanent establishment must complete local registration and obtain a Spanish NIF-VAT (Número de Identificación Fiscal a efectos de IVA) by submitting the corresponding Form 036 or through the AEAT electronic register, attaching the foreign incorporation certificate, a current power of attorney, and, where applicable, a certificate of tax residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Spanish SL is an opaque entity subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) as a resident taxpayer on its worldwide income, without application of any pass-through or transparent treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spanish law does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box regime. The SL is automatically treated as a fully taxable corporation. Available elective mechanisms include: (i) group tax consolidation election for resident group parent companies under the Corporate Income Tax Act; (ii) special reduced-rate and accelerated depreciation elections for small enterprises; (iii) optional quarterly VAT refund scheme under the EU Special Scheme for small businesses in limited cases; (iv) election to use the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) and IOSS schemes for B2C distances sales and digital services; (v) application of the patent box regime and R&D tax incentive elections. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available because Spain implements mandatory ATAD anti-hybrid rules without optionality.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), the Spanish Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 0 EUR (no general VAT registration threshold). Any taxable person performing on-going economic activity in mainland Spain must register with the AEAT before commencing supplies. For intra-EU distance sales to non-established taxable persons and to Spanish consumers, the optional OSS threshold is 10,000 EUR per calendar year, but a Spanish-established SL must be VAT-registered from inception regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates electronic invoicing between businesses and professionals under the 'Crea y Crece' Act (Ley 18/2022), with implementation of the VeriFactu system providing standardized statement delivery and a QR code for invoice authenticity. Large taxpayers whose taxable turnover exceeds EUR 100 million, and members of VAT groups, must operate the Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII), filing all VAT ledger details to the AEAT through machine-to-machine SOAP/REST web services in near real-time (within four business days after the invoice is issued). No fiscal stamping of invoices occurs before issuance; the AEAT receives data post-invoice and validates the authenticity of the electronic record.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Spanish VAT law, supplies of goods physically exported to third countries or Ceuta and Melilla are zero-rated (art. 21 Ley 21/1992). Proof of export is satisfied by a customs export declaration and transport documentation. Services that are directly related to export or import of goods may also be zero-rated. For digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements, zero-rating is not normally applicable; instead, the relevant supply is removed from the scope of Spanish VAT by place-of-supply rules when the customer is a business established outside Spain (reverse charge) or, in B2C situations, when the recipient is a private consumer established outside the EU and the services are deemed supplied in that territory. To rely on this non-Spanish treatment, the supplier must obtain adequate proof of the customer's establishment or residence, such as VAT registration number, billing address, IP address geolocation, bank details of the payment account, or other relevant commercial evidence.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) applies elevated audit scrutiny to claims of VAT exemption or zero-rating on exports and to cross-border services that are positioned outside the scope of Spanish VAT. Where insufficient evidentiary documentation is maintained, the AEAT retroactively assesses the omitted VAT, plus late-payment interest and surcharges, and imposes administrative penalties ranging from 50% to 150% of the tax undercharged, depending on whether the infringement is considered serious or very serious (Ley General Tributaria, arts. 178-191). For false invoicing or fraudulent use of fictitious export documentation, civil penalties are escalated and criminal prosecution for tax fraud can be pursued, carrying prison terms and additional fines. Recoveries and clawback assessments may cover the standard four-year limitation period, which is extended in cases of complex concealment or prior interposition of legal proceedings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (the Bank of Spain), operating jointly with the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business for foreign-exchange and capital-movement purposes; the foreign-exchange administration functions are allocated to the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCI) under the State Secretariat for Trade; the anti-money-laundering supervisory component is executed by SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención de Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias). The legal foundation is Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union on the free movement of capital, Royal Decree 664/1999 of 23 April on foreign investments, Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering, and the Bank of Spain's statistical reporting circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full capital and current-account convertibility applies because Spain is a Euro-area member state and the euro is unrestricted legal tender. No exchange-control authorisation, registration, or repatriation permit is required for current transactions (digital subscription fees, advertising revenue, royalties, dividends, interest, service fees) or for capital movements (direct investment, shareholder loans, securities transactions). Profit remittance is blocked only by ordinary tax compliance, not by FX regulation: a Spanish Sociedad de Limitada (SL) may freely distribute dividends and payable reserves to non-resident shareholders, subject to the statutory corporate income tax, withholding tax on distributions (19% standard, reduced under tax treaties or exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive), and anti-abuse rules. Practical treasury hurdles remain in bank-level documentary scrutiny: the receiving bank must justify the economic substance of inward remittances and the payer must produce the standard Spanish corporate identifiers (NIF) and residence certificates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to sell export proceeds to the central bank. For the digital magazine publishing scope, subscription, sponsorship, and advertising proceeds received from non-residents in USD, GBP, or other currencies may be credited to freely available EUR accounts or converted at market rates at the SL's discretion. The only compulsory obligations are: (i) proper invoicing with VAT documentation for cross-border services, (ii) statistical balance-of-payments declaration to the Banco de España under Circular 2/2021 whenever non-cash settlements with non-residents equal or exceed EUR 50,000 per month (or as otherwise thresholded), and (iii) retention of the underlying commercial contracts and payment-flow evidence for tax, customs, and SEPBLAC inspection. No special export-proceeds account, no Central-Bank-nominated buying obligation, and no prior approval applies to ISIC 5813 operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (current account) plus optional Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (current account) plus digital treasury self-service
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account for notarised capital injections
Operational Account (current account) for premium relationship treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EEA-authorized electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passported into Spain under the EU payment-services framework (Law 21/2011 on Electronic Money and the transposition of PSD2). These digital banks may lawfully hold euro balances and issue Spanish IBANs; however, relying exclusively on Stripe, AdSense Payout, or an offshore EMI is not advisable, because the Spanish tax authorities and commercial counterparties expect cash management through a domestic bank account for VAT (Modelo 303) and corporate tax (Modelo 100) payments, and because maintaining foreign financial accounts above EUR 50,000 triggers the Modelo 720 information-reporting obligation and the automatic exchange-of-information regime. Feasibility rating: Low for non-EEA offshore EMIs or 'digital banks' licensed in third-country financial centres (such as Caribbean or Middle-East fintech entities): under Spanish law they are not authorised to provide electronic-money services to Spanish residents unless they obtain a Banco de España licence or a valid EU passport; Spanish Tier-1 banks will frequently reject or suspend correspondent flows originating from such institutions, and treasury funds parked there face substantial tax-opacity and KYC-rejection risk. The recommended structure is to use a Spanish Tier-1 operational account as the single treasury spine and treat Stripe/AdSense as receivables-collection rails only, with daily sweeps into Spain.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish Tier-1 banks normally require at least one physical compliance interview and in-branch signature of the appointed legal representative (administrador solidario or apoderado) before opening a corporate account, particularly where the beneficial owners are non-resident. Fully remote opening is available only in limited cases using the Spanish electronic ID (DNIe) or a qualified electronic certificate and is reserved for natural-person domestic entrepreneurs; for a non-resident-owned digital magazine SL, the bank's underwriting committee will require an in-person meeting at a designated branch or, exceptionally, a high-grade video-identity verification with the original documents couriered beforehand. The mandated KYC package includes: (i) notarised and apostilled deed of incorporation of the SL and deed of appointment of the administrator; (ii) sworn Spanish translation of all non-Spanish corporate documents; (iii) passport and NIE or foreigner tax identification number of each director and ultimate beneficial owner; (iv) proof of registered address in Spain (lease or title deed) and evidence of actual editorial operations; and (v) a face-to-face interview with the beneficial owner or, if impossible, with the attorney holding a general power (poder general) granted before a Spanish notary with authority clauses covering banking onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: An entirely non-resident ownership chain (e.g., Latin-American parent shareholders holding 100% of the Spanish SL) combined with a new-economy business model that has no physical inventory or local workforce, creating an elevated classification concern during customer due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certification from the Spanish Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) showing the incorporation, share capital, registered office, and current appointment of directors; statutory filing in the Registro de Titularidades Reales identifying all ultimate beneficial owners; two years of certified or audited financial statements; personal valid passports and NIE/TIE numbers of every director; sworn declaration of source of wealth and source of funds; a commercial business plan evidencing the digital magazine platform, sponsorship pipeline, and content-licence agreements; and tax-residence certificates or treaty profiles for every non-resident shareholder to demonstrate legitimate cross-border ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, high-volume inward payment flows from global e-payment platforms (Stripe and Google AdSense) that generate a treasury pattern inconsistent with a traditional publishing company and could be suspected to aggregate third-party proceeds or conceal advertising rebates and comission arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed business-model memorandum explaining the digital magazine distribution value chain, revenue recognition policies, and the role of sponsored media placements; global platform account statements from Stripe and Google AdSense showing the merchant identity, settlement volumes, and payout frequency; monthly payout reconciliation reports between platform records and the Spanish bank account; sample executed contracts with advertisers, content partners, and freelance contributors; consistent tax filings (Modelo 303 for VAT and Modelo 100 for corporate income) matching the treasury flow; and the bank's annual enhanced-review questionnaire answered with supporting documents demonstrating a low-risk standard customer rating.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection by non-resident shareholders immediately followed by outward disbursements to foreign freelancers or technology suppliers, a pattern that may resemble layering or round-tripping of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and registered minutes confirming the capital increase or shareholder loan, filed with the Registro Mercantil; the post-notarisation foreign-investment declaration to the DGCI/Registro de Inversiones Exteriores; executed intercompany loan agreements or equity-subscription agreements at arm's length terms; a complete invoice-and-payment trail for every outbound disbursement (invoice number, NIF/CIF of the payee, bank-statement cross-reference, and contract reference); an explanation of the economic purpose of each outward payment (e.g., editorial fees, software licences); and a board-authorised treasury policy prohibiting cash withdrawals, bearer instruments, or routing through unlicensed third-country intermediaries.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound protocol for capital injection into the ES_SL: (1) formalise the capital increase, share premium, or subscription in a Spanish notary public deed and file it at the Registro Mercantil; (2) file the post-investment declaration with the DGCI foreign-investment register within one month after notarisation as required by Royal Decree 664/1999; (3) transmit the funds by SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank, denominating in EUR to avoid intermediate conversion, using the Spanish bank's BIC and a clear remittance reference that identifies the transaction as 'ampliación de capital' or 'préstamo de accionistas'; (4) instruct the remitter to include the Bank of Spain statistical concept classification for direct investment or intra-group financial lending in the payment narrative so the receiving bank can correctly assign the balance-of-payments code; (5) have the beneficial owner's name, NIF, and shareholder identification appear exactly as in the notarised deed; and (6) if the amount is EUR 10,000 or more, ensure the funds move only through bank-to-bank channels, never cash or bearer drafts. No prior exchange-control licence is required, and the funds become immediately available for treasury operations once credited; the bank will be satisfied by the notary deed and the registered foreign-investment declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the ISIC 5813 digital magazine and sponsored-media scope, the operative clearing rails are: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) through TARGET2 for euro payments within the SEPA zone, including instant settlements for freelancer and technology-vendor disbursements; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA or cross-currency payments (USD, GBP) to overseas editorial contributors, advertisers, software platforms, and LatAm partner entities, using cover payment in the beneficiary's settlement currency; and (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary LC) remain technically available but are functionally inapt for recurring digital service payments and should be avoided for open-account content licensing and sponsorship settlements. Every outbound payment must be supported by a proper invoice nomenclature, state the exact business purpose (e.g., 'remuneración por servicios editoriales', 'cuotas de licencia de software', 'pago por servicios de publicidad'), and be matched against the vendor's Spanish NIF/VAT number where applicable to substantiate VAT deductibility. The SL should reconcile SWIFT FIN acknowledgements or MT103 confirmations against the accounts payable ageing report monthly.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EU/EMIR-compliant deliverable outright FX forwards in EUR/USD and EUR/GBP with tenors up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with a Spanish Tier-1 bank; the SL acts as a non-financial counterparty below the EMIR clearing threshold, so no mandatory clearing or bilateral margining applies, though the bank may request a transactional margin in low-limit treasury engagements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-convertible or restricted Latin-American currencies (e.g., Chilean peso, Colombian peso, Peruvian sol) used to hedge advertising rebates and sponsorship inflows from LatAm markets where deliverable conversion is impossible or administratively burdensome; NDFs are settled net in EUR/USD without physical exchange of the underlying currency.

Cross-currency swaps combining a spot FX conversion and a forward re-exchange (FX swap) to bridge temporarily the USD balances held in Stripe/AdSense settlement accounts against EUR payroll obligations, thereby managing cash timing mismatches without incurring overnight currency exposure.

Plain-vanilla European FX options (EUR call/USD put and USD call/EUR put) purchased on an upfront premium basis to protect the SL's projected USD advertising revenue against adverse EUR/USD movement while retaining upside participation.

FX spot block trades executed via the bank's e-FX portal on a T+2/T+3 settlement basis for just-in-time payment of international licensing fees and for immediate conversion of collected platform proceeds, subject to the bank's corporate dealing limit and tested revenue logic.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) and Management Report (Memoria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following approval by the General Meeting of Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 3,000 euros per year of delay; potential company strike-off if not rectified

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual turnover exceeds 2 million euros, total assets exceed 1 million euros, or average number of employees exceeds 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) for non-listed companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual UBO confirmation filing; update beneficial ownership register upon any changes in ownership or control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100-500 USD for Spanish registered office; 300-1,500 USD for foreign registered agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-3,000 USD if independent audit is required based on thresholds

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); reduced rates apply to newly created SLs: 15% on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base and 20% on the excess, for the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base (LIS Art. 29.1)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for digital magazine publishing. Available relief: R&D and technological innovation tax credits (LIS Art. 35: 25% of qualifying R&D expenses, 42% on excess; 12% for patent box with 60% exemption on qualifying IP income); digital services tax (Law 4/2020) only applies to groups with global revenues above EUR 750M and EU revenues above EUR 250M, thus outside the scope of the SL. New entity relief: 15%/20% reduced rates described above.
stage_6.narrative_addendum: Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, but the annual offset is capped at 70% of the positive taxable base for entities with net turnover below EUR 20 million (25% cap for turnover above EUR 60 million). A one-year reduced-rate regime (15%) obviously no carryforward—I'll word correctly.
